message: Root-caused the 12-byte leak: mid-function continuations are emitted as EMPTY stubs
note: Traced esp through sub_002155B0 -> sub_00123590 -> sub_00202CC0 with probes. sub_00123600 never runs (eax==0). The leak is entirely in sub_00202CC0. Ghidra: FUN_00202cc0 is ONE 254-byte function (0x202CC0-0x202DBD); the lifter split it into fragments CC0/CE1/D14 which push but contain ZERO pops, then tail-call sub_00202D87/D89 - which live in recomp_stubs_unresolved.c as EMPTY BODIES ('not detected'). whatis.py confirms 0x202D87 is real .text code. So the continuation, including the pop esi/pop ebx/ret epilogue, never executes. Arithmetic matches exactly: 4 (dummy retaddr from sub_00123590) + 8 (ebx,esi in sub_00202CC0) = 12 bytes, and esi is never restored -> the caller's esi is destroyed. 3205 such stubs exist. This is the class behind esp drift, callee-saved corruption and the stack-address ICALL targets.

message: Narrow seed did NOT fix the leak; real cause is dropped fall-through edges (1005 functions)
note: Seeded sub_00202D87/D89 and removed their stubs: build clean, but probes show the leak UNCHANGED (esp still -16 where -4 is due, esi still clobbered) - the chain never reaches them. Built trace_stubs.py: armed all 3203 unresolved stubs to report themselves; only TEN execute during boot, and none in the 0x202Cxx/Dxx range. Real cause found by reading sub_00202CE1's tail: it ends on RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE with NO return, no epilogue, no esp adjustment. The original falls through to 0x202D14; the lifter split there and never emitted the edge, so control falls off the end of the C function and the pop esi/pop ebx/ret never runs. 4 (dummy retaddr) + 8 (ebx,esi) = exactly the 12 measured. Built find_dropped_fallthrough.py: 1005 functions (3.79%) do this. First version reported 14.28% - false positives from trailing #undef lines after the real return; validated by hand and fixed. Seed kept (inert: 54/heap 8/no crash held; failed_icalls 1->2 because real code now runs where an empty stub used to silently succeed).

message: Root-cause the 200-call crash: the subsystem table at 0x005BB700 is never written
note: sub_002235D0 (the class registrar) reads ecx = MEM32(eax*4 + 0x5BB700) with the index from 0x5BC544, gets NULL, and faults on ecx-0x88. ReVa: 249 references to DAT_005bb700 and EVERY ONE is isWrite:false - nothing in the discovered code ever populates that table. esp is healthy across all 200 kernel calls (stays in 0x00F7Fxxx, largest swings are legitimate +/-448 frame allocations), so this is NOT stack drift. find_icall_esp_saves --live reports only 1 live site worth 20 bytes, far too small to matter. Next: find what populates 0x005BB700 - likely an undiscovered constructor or static initializer, i.e. the find_missing_functions.py data-pointer case rather than the control-flow case.
